the identification of genetic abnormalities in lymphomas, and the correlation of these genetic changes with clinical parameters.
the development of new methods to identify the genetic alterations that occur in human cancers, and with the identification of the genes that are affected by those alterations.
the molecular cytogenetic characterization of a panel of diffuse large B-cell (DLBCL) lymphomas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cytogenetic profile and level of instability of DLBCL, as determined by SKY, is more extensive and complex than that determined by G-banding.
SKY is a powerful technique that can identify new recurring breakpoints, new translocations, and new regions of gain and losses, and that can also provide new clinical associations.

SKY has identified 13 new breakpoints not previously detected by G-banding; has detected a total of 10 breakpoints underrepresented by G-band analysis, which includes 4 previously unrecognized breakpoints; has identified four new translocations, and has detected 4 new regions of gain and 3 regions of loss.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

SKY analysis of DLBCL is a powerful tool for identifying new recurring translocations, new breakpoints, and new regions of gain and/or loss, which will facilitate gene discovery as well clinical correlation analysis.
SKY is more sensitive and specific than G-banding in the analysis of DLBCL and that SKY provides a better understanding of the genetic heterogeneity of DLBCL.

SKY analysis is a powerful tool for defining the cytogenetic landscape of DLBCL and for identifying new recurring aberrations, translocations, regions of gain and/or loss, and new clinical associations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
spectral karyotyping is a more comprehensive method for analyzing the karyotype of diffuse large B-cell (DLBCL) lymphoma cells.

SKY is a powerful tool for characterizing complex aberrations in cancer cells, including DLBCL, and that SKY can be used as an adjunct to G-banding for gene discovery and for identification of new clinical correlations.

spectral karyotyping is an important tool to complement G-banding for the characterization of chromosomal instability and to facilitate gene discovery and clinical correlation in diffuse large B cell lymphoma.
